name: Odilon Redon
bio: Odilon Redon was a French Symbolist draughtsman, printmaker, and painter.

paintings.title: The Cyclops (Redon)
paintings.story: The Cyclops is a symbolist painting by Odilon Redon that depicts the myth of the love of Polyphemus for the nymph Galatea. It was painted in oil on cardboard, then mounted on wood, and is now in the Kröller-Müller Museum in the Netherlands. The painting has been variously dated between 1898 and 1914.
facts: It appears Polyphemus has hidden himself from the nymph behind the rocky terrain, too shy to directly confront her "helpless" form.
Galatea is shown asleep on the lower right, her naked body blending into the flowery hill slope.

Vase of Flowers
paintings.story: Known for his dark, velvety charcoal drawings and lithographs, Redon began working predominantly in oil and pastel after 1900, thus enlisting color in his explorations of the world of dreams and the imagination. Like other Symbolists, Redon searched for alternative experiences beyond the rational logic of Naturalism and Impressionism. He used his knowledge of botany as a starting point for this painting, but infused the flowers with heightened luminosity and sensuous form.

Symbolic Head
paintings.story: One of Redon's favorite themes of the 1880s and 1890s was a human head depicted in profile. This motif came from his representations of severed heads, often carried aloft on wings, published in the artist's first album of prints, Dans le rêve (1879). In these images, the separation of the head from the body symbolizes the spirit released from the material world. It also suggests a metaphor for abandoning physical reality for the inner realm of dreams, fantasy, and poetic reverie. This painting conveys the idea of inward-turning vision by framing the head in a series of collapsing rectangles. Redon isolated the head even further by painting a horizontal rectangle or "ledge" over the lower part of the figure's body, which originally extended to the bottom edge of the composition. Conservation analysis confirms that the figure is a woman wearing a helmet and holding a green staff in her right hand. However, her exact identity is not known, largely because after altering the crest and other aspects of the helmet, Redon abandoned the painting in an unresolved state.

paintings.title: Pond in les Landes
paintings.story: Pond in les Landes Oil on paper on panel "Redon was best known for his imaginative compositions and brightly colored still lifes, yet he also painted naturalistic landscapes. Les Landes, a large area in southwest France, once consisted of a mix of unfertile sandy ground and boggy marshes. Following drainage projects in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, les Landes now supports a vast pine forest."
